title: keyword_matches whole_word uses byte-level boundary check on lowercased UTF-8
description: src/posting.rs:200-232. keyword_matches() lowercases both strings, then uses is_ascii_alphanumeric() for word boundary detection on the lowercased bytes. This works correctly for ASCII hashtag/keyword patterns (the typical case), but would fail to identify word boundaries around non-ASCII alphabetic characters (e.g. accented letters). The function should document this limitation: 'Word boundary detection is ASCII-only; non-ASCII alphanumeric characters are treated as non-word characters.' This matches Mastodon's behavior, so it's correct but not obvious.
